title: Hagelloch 1861, fitted: the time to the rash nearly fixed and the prodrome's last 2 days weighted apart

source.citation: Pfeilsticker A. Beiträge zur Pathologie der Masern mit besonderer Berücksichtigung der statistischen Verhältnisse. Tübingen: Eberhard-Karls-Universität; 1863.
source.read: OCR text of the incubation chapter, 2026-11-18

evidence.quote: dass die Zeit von der Ansteckung bis zur Eruption … constant 14 Tage sei (that the time from infection to the rash is a constant 14 days)
evidence.working: Infection to the rash 12 to 13 days, less a prodrome of 2: 10 to 11 days. 12 to 13 is the record's latent period (median 8.5, experiment 199) and prodrome (mean 4) together, held nearly fixed as the rule of 1863 holds it fixed.
evidence.note: Pfeilsticker's 14 days is from infection; the model's day of infection is the day of transmission, and the record's intervals give 12 to 13. A sensitivity runs others.

evidence.quote: transmissible from 4 days before through 4 days after rash onset
evidence.working: The day of the rash and the 4 days after it: 5 days. With the 4-day prodrome, 9 infectious days in all, as in the Pink Book set.
evidence.note: Not in the record: nothing marks when a child stopped being infectious. Kept from the Pink Book.

evidence.working: Fitted 2026-11-22 by scripts/abm-hagelloch-fit.mjs --join: the three probabilities and the two weights together, on a grid of 5 × 6 × 6 × 4 × 4 points at 100 runs each, then 7 × 7 × 7 × 3 × 3 around the best at 300; the Poisson deviance of the record's rashes per day (days 0 to 89 from the index child's) against the model's mean, the school shut on Sundays. Best 0.261; within 4 of the best's deviance, 0.082 to 0.33.
evidence.note: A fit to one outbreak, not a property of measles.
